pr.title: Refresh the Projector section of AGENTS.md and the site workflow
pr.head: 359b0d4fcadc9dd0ddb07de6ce58da63076bdeff

summary: This repository uses Projector to record project plans, review pull requests, and publish a review site. This change brings two pieces of generated repository configuration forward: the instructions that sessions follow and the workflow that deploys the site.

The new instructions tell every session to open pull requests as drafts and never to mark its own draft ready, on the understanding that a review marks the draft ready once its head is clean. The site also deploys when a same-repository pull request closes, so a merged or closed review stops appearing open without waiting for an unrelated deployment.

cards.title: What the review checked
cards.html:
• Both changed files were read in full. The workflow matches what the installed Projector writes, byte for byte.
  • One finding is open. The draft rule in AGENTS.md describes a review loop that Projector has since changed. Projector 0.9.8 never moves a pull request out of draft, and its repository review waits until the author marks a draft ready with project review ready.
  • project check validates the plans. It warns that instruction version 4 is older than version 29 from the installed command.
  • All text outside the Projector markers is unchanged.
  • The close-event deployment needs a real GitHub event after this workflow reaches the default branch.

groups.title: Open pull requests as drafts and build stacks
groups.kicker: Repository instructions apply the draft and stack conventions to every session.
intro: AGENTS.md gives sessions the repository’s working rules. The new section tells each session to open pull requests as drafts, including each layer of a stack, which is a series of dependent pull requests. It also says that a review marks a draft ready when its head is clean, so a session must never mark its own draft ready.

For dependent work, the instructions use gh stack to carry a fix from the branch that introduced it into the branches above. Base-branch chaining and merges remain the fallback when that tool is unavailable.

files.note: Adds the draft and dependent-work conventions inside the generated Projector section.

checks.text: Compared the text before and after the Projector markers against the merge base; it is unchanged.
This update targets version 4 of the instructions. The installed Projector command ships version 29, so project check still reports instructions-outdated.

Agents that follow this paragraph leave every pull request in draft, so the repository review never picks it up. Projector 0.9.8 never marks a draft ready, and its repository review announces nothing for a draft until the author marks it ready with project review ready, the step this paragraph forbids. Refreshing the section with the installed project init writes version 29, which tells agents to mark a draft ready once their work is done.

groups.title: Refresh the site when a pull request closes
groups.kicker: A close event deploys the default branch for same-repository work.
intro: The Projector site lists review summaries and each pull request’s state. Its workflow now listens for pull_request_target with the closed activity, which covers both merged pull requests and those closed without merging.

The publish job skips pull requests whose head belongs to another repository. Those fork events also receive a separate concurrency group, so they do not replace a pending deployment in the shared pages group.

files.note: Adds a close-event trigger, skips fork pull requests, and separates their concurrency groups.

checks.text: Traced the site action to actions/checkout with no ref override. GitHub documents that pull_request_target uses the default branch, so this trigger does not execute the pull request’s head.
Read the job condition against same-repository and fork close events: same-repository events publish, and fork events skip.
